title: Behavior When Partial Configuration Available: Fail Open, Fail Closed and Best Effort Policies
aliases: Timed out while waiting for config

prose.label: The three modes.
prose.text: {{modes}} The page describes Fail Closed as blocking traffic, and also lists a log action named for a bypass under Fail Closed {{divergence:fail-closed-bypassed}}.

prose.label: In the logs.
prose.text: {{logging}} The log side is in [[zia.logs.firewall-records]] and [[zia.insights.logs]].
The page this setting sits on is routed in [[zia.advanced-settings]].

why-config-is-fetched.statement: When a new session from an organization first reaches the Zero Trust Exchange, the Service Edge connects to the Zscaler Central Authority to get the policy configuration in a hierarchy, starting with the organization policy, followed by location policy and user policy. Policy enforcement for traffic from an authenticated user or a known location requires the Service Edge to have the organization's full configurations, including security policies, locations and users, downloaded from the Central Authority.

quotes: When a new session from an organization arrives for the first time at the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) for processing, the Service Edge connects to the Zscaler Central Authority (CA) to get the policy configuration in a hierarchy, starting with the organization policy, followed by location policy and user policy.

When traffic from an authenticated user or a known location arrives at a Service Edge, the policy enforcement requires the Service Edge to have the organization's full configurations, including security policies, locations, and users, downloaded from the CA.

when-partial.statement: In rare scenarios caused by transient network disruptions or delays, a Service Edge might be unable to retrieve the full configurations from the Central Authority for a given session and might need to operate with incomplete or cached tenant, user or location configurations. The page calls this extremely unlikely under normal operating conditions and temporary, typically occurring when there is brief connection latency to the Central Authority as a new session reaches a Service Edge that has not finished retrieving its configuration. The Behavior When Partial Configuration Available setting defines how security policies are enforced in that state.

quotes: In rare scenarios caused by transient network disruptions or delays, the Service Edge might be unable to retrieve the full configurations from the CA for a given session and might need to operate with incomplete or cached tenant, user, or location configurations.
The Behavior When Partial Configuration Available setting allows you to define how security policies are enforced when a Service Edge operates with incomplete configurations.
A Service Edge having only partial configurations is extremely unlikely under normal operating conditions.

The partial configuration state is temporary and typically occurs when there is brief connection latency to the CA as a new session from an organization reaches a Service Edge, before that Service Edge has finished retrieving its configuration from the CA.

modes.statement: The setting has three modes. Fail Open, the default, skips policy evaluation for a session when complete configurations are not available and lets the traffic pass. Fail Closed blocks traffic unless a complete configuration is available to apply, at the risk of some sessions occasionally being blocked. Best Effort Policies applies the most specific policy rules available by falling back to a previously acquired policy.

quotes: Fail Open: If complete configurations are not available, policy evaluation is skipped for that session and the traffic is allowed to pass through. This is the default mode and ensures maximum connectivity.

Fail Closed: Prioritizes strict security by blocking traffic unless a complete configuration is available to apply. This mode should be selected for the strictest application of policy rules on every session at the risk of some sessions occasionally being blocked.
Best Effort Policies: Applies the most specific policy rules available by falling back to a previously acquired policy.

best-effort-fallback.statement: In the Best Effort Policies mode, the policy falls back to a global location (Org Default) or a general user type (Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions) for a session when a more specific admin-configured user or location policy is not available. For rules with explicit location or user criteria, the Org Default location or the Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions user, or both, must be added to the rule so it can match during evaluation and trigger the fallback; rules that match any locations or users do not require them.

quotes: In the Best Effort Policies mode, the policy falls back to using a global location (Org Default) or a general user type (Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions) to apply to a session if a more specific admin-configured user or location policy is not available.

To fully implement this mode, you must additionally add the Org Default location or the Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions user, or both, to policy rules that include explicit location or user criteria (i.e., if it is configured to match specific locations or users).
This is required so that the rule can match the Org Default location or the Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions user during evaluation and trigger the fallback.
Rules that are configured to match any locations or users do not require this location or user type to be added.

best-effort-objects.statement: The Org Default location and the Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions user can be used in all Web and Firewall policy rules that support user- and location-based conditions. The mode can be changed from Best Effort Policies to other options only when no policy rules reference them. On the Locations page, only Enforce Firewall Control and Enable IPS Control can be edited on Org Default, Firewall Control must be enabled for Org Default for Firewall policies to use it, and it does not support sublocations. The Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions user can be viewed only in policy rule conditions and is not editable.

quotes: The Org Default location and the Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions user can be used in all Web and Firewall policy rules that support user- and location-based conditions.

Consistent with that approach, you can change from Best Effort Policies to other options only when no policy rules currently reference the Org Default location or the Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions user.
You can view the Org Default location on the Locations page and edit very limited parameters (only Enforce Firewall Control and Enable IPS Control).
The Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions user can be viewed only in policy rule conditions and is not editable.
Ensure that Firewall Control is enabled for the Org Default location to apply Firewall policies using this location.
The Org Default location does not support adding sublocations.

scope-and-session.statement: The selected mode applies to both secure web gateway and firewall traffic. Policy evaluation begins when a session is established and uses the policy available at that moment. When only an incomplete policy is available at session establishment and Best Effort Policies or Fail Open is active, the available policy is used for the entire session, and subsequent sessions trigger new attempts to retrieve the complete policy configuration.

quotes: The selected mode applies to both secure web gateway and firewall traffic.
Policy evaluation always begins when a session is established and uses the policy available at that moment.

If only an incomplete policy configuration is available at the time of session establishment and either Best Effort Policies or Fail Open mode is active (i,e., the session was allowed even though the policy for that session was incomplete), then the available policy is used for the entire duration of that session.
Subsequent sessions trigger new attempts to retrieve the complete policy configuration.

logging.statement: When Best Effort Policies or Fail Closed mode is used, the policy actions Bypassed due to missing config and Timed out while waiting for config might additionally appear in Firewall logs under specific circumstances. In Best Effort Policies the actual authenticated user is logged (if Z-Tunnel 2.0 or cookie authentication is used) even if the policy was applied using the Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions user; if the user identity is unknown (for example Z-Tunnel 1.0), the transaction is logged for that user. The traffic origin location is logged correctly even if Org Default was used. These transactions are made distinct by the Configuration column set to Partial in Web logs, a distinction not currently available in Firewall and DNS logs.

quotes: When Best Effort Policies or Fail Closed mode is used, the following policy actions might additionally appear in Firewall logs under specific circumstances: Bypassed due to missing config and Timed out while waiting for config.

In the Best Effort Policies mode, the actual authenticated user information (if Z-Tunnel 2.0 or cookie authentication is used) is logged to improve traffic source visibility, even if the policy was applied using the Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions user.
If the user identity is unknown (e.g., uses Z-Tunnel 1.0), the transaction is logged for the Miscellaneous Unauthenticated Transactions user.
Similarly, the traffic origin location is logged correctly even if the Org Default location was used for the policy application.
The transactions are, however, made distinct using the Configuration column value set to Partial in Web logs.
This distinction using the Configuration column is not currently available in Firewall and DNS logs.

fail-closed-bypassed.summary: Fail Closed is described as blocking traffic unless a complete configuration is available, yet the same page says a Firewall log action Bypassed due to missing config might appear when Fail Closed is used.

quotes: Fail Closed: Prioritizes strict security by blocking traffic unless a complete configuration is available to apply.

positions.says: Fail Closed blocks traffic unless a complete configuration is available to apply.

quotes: When Best Effort Policies or Fail Closed mode is used, the following policy actions might additionally appear in Firewall logs under specific circumstances: Bypassed due to missing config and Timed out while waiting for config.

positions.says: With Best Effort Policies or Fail Closed, Firewall logs might show Bypassed due to missing config and Timed out while waiting for config.

quotes: This implicit rule action is logged when the Service Edge for Internet & SaaS (ZIA) fails to establish a connection with the Zscaler Central Authority (CA), resulting in the traffic flow passing through Zscaler Firewall or DNS without policy application.

positions.says: Bypassed due to missing config is logged when the Service Edge fails to connect to the Central Authority, and the traffic flow passes through Firewall or DNS without policy application.

fail-closed-bypassed.impact: The Policy Reasons definition describes a bypass that passes traffic without policy application, while Fail Closed is described as blocking; neither page says which circumstances produce a bypass action under Fail Closed, so a Bypassed due to missing config record cannot be read as proof that Fail Closed allowed the traffic or that another mode was selected.
